item.title: Application of Isatoic Anhydride‐Modified Ceramic Catalytic Membrane in the C2‐Arylation of Indoles
item.description: Using isatoic anhydride and KH550, a recyclable Pd-loaded ceramic catalytic membrane was developed. Systematic investigation of loading temperature on silane coupling agent growth (using Pd content as criterion) identified 90 °C as optimal. The Pd-ABA-KH550-CM-90 membrane showed stable catalysis over 12 cycles without Pd leaching, high activity in gram-scale drug synthesis, highlighting its potential for sustainable catalysis.

item.title: Aliovalent Cl Substitution Modulates Oxygen‐Vacancy‐Related Defect States in Bi2O2S Toward Efficient Photocatalytic CO2‐to‐CO Conversion
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Aliovalent Cl substitution modulates oxygen-vacancy-related defect states and reconstructs the local electronic environment of layered Bi2O2S. The coupled dopant–defect interaction promotes charge redistribution and differentiated adsorption of CO2 and H2O at local surface environments, contributing to enhanced photocatalytic CO2-to-CO conversion. The optimized Cl-BOS-0.6 achieves an 18.6-fold enhancement in CO evolution rate over pristine Bi2O2S.


Pristine Bi2O2S suffers from pronounced surface inertness and inefficient utilization of photogenerated charge carriers in photocatalytic CO2 reduction. To address this limitation, an aliovalent Cl-for-S substitution strategy is employed. Owing to the comparable ionic sizes of Cl− and S2−, Cl incorporation largely preserves the host crystal framework while modulating oxygen-vacancy-related defect states, modifying the electronic structure, and promoting photogenerated charge separation and migration. As a result, the optimized Cl-BOS-0.6 catalyst achieves a CO evolution rate of 59.6 μmol g−1·h−1, corresponding to an approximately 18.6-fold enhancement over pristine Bi2O2S, together with good stability and CO selectivity. In situ spectroscopic characterizations and density functional theory calculations further indicate a coupled dopant–defect effect that promotes local charge redistribution and differentiated adsorption of CO2 and H2O, thereby facilitating efficient and selective photocatalytic CO2-to-CO conversion. This work provides a viable strategy for regulating the local electronic structure and defect chemistry of Bi2O2S-based photocatalysts and offers new insight into the rational design of efficient CO2 photoreduction materials.

item.title: Metal‐Catalyzed Transformations of Carbon Dioxide Toward the Production of Commodity Chemicals
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

This perspective highlights how transition-metal catalysis can enable the synthesis of economically attractive CO2-derived commodity chemicals. By transforming waste CO2 into acrylic acid, cyclic carbonates, and other valuable products, these strategies provide a practical route for simultaneous CO2 sequestration and valorization, helping to align sustainable chemical manufacturing with industrial feasibility.


This perspective examines advances in catalytic methods for converting CO2 into value-added commodity chemicals through a future-facing research and development-focused viewpoint. As such, select examples that we identify as representative of the field in both mature and underdeveloped technologies are discussed. Transition-metal catalysis has enabled progress toward the production of acrylic acid derivatives, methylmalonic acids, and cyclic carbonates, despite CO2’s inherent stability. In contrast, other promising transformations, such as the synthesis of amino acids from CO2, remain limited by high costs, narrow substrate scope, and poor stereocontrol. Overall, CO2 utilization offered significant potential as an economic means for sustainable chemical manufacturing while highlighting the need for further catalytic innovation.

item.title: Green Synthesis of Functional γ‐Lactams via Metal‐Free Promoted Selective Reductive Amination/Cyclization
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

An efficient and high chemoselective reductive amination/cyclization to access functional γ-lactams, including isoindolinones, pyrrolidones, and oxazino isoindolinones were well developed by HBpin-promoted system under mild conditions (metal-free, green solvent, and low temperature) with tolerated functional rings and unsaturated groups.


Developing a “green” synthetic method to functional γ-lactam is essential due to their significant importance to numerous fields. In this work, we developed an efficient and highly chemoselective reductive amination/cyclization to access isoindolinones and pyrrolidones from 2-formylbenzoic and levulinic acid with anilines by a metal-free and HBpin reaction system under mild conditions with tolerated functional rings and unsaturated groups. In addition, various oxazino isoindolinones were easily synthesized from substituted 3-aminopropanols via HBpin-promoted reductive amination/cyclization under mild conditions. Moreover, HBpin demonstrates the dual roles of promoter and reducing reagent. Density functional theory calculations were performed to verify the mechanism of HBpin-promoted reductive amination/cyclization.

item.title: Selective Photoinduced α‐Amino C(sp3)–H Alkylation Mediated by NHC–Borane
item.description: Herein, we report a selective photoinduced functionalization of α-amino C(sp3)─H bonds mediated by NHC–boranes. This reaction proceeds efficiently without the need for any external radical initiator or photoredox catalyst. Mechanistic studies reveal that the reaction proceeds via an efficient radical chain, featuring the formation of an aryl radical driven by a boryl-mediated XAT and a subsequent 1,5-HAT as key steps. The method demonstrates broad functional group tolerance, providing a practical route for the synthesis of nitrogen-containing molecules.

item.title: Enzyme@Silicone: A Versatile Combo for Robust Synthetic Biocatalysis?
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Silicone-based polymers are versatile materials for enzyme immobilization, offering unique advantages such as chemical inertness, thermal stability, and tunable morphology. This review highlights their applications in synthetic biocatalysis, from batch to continuous processes, and addresses key challenges such as mass transport limitations and scalability. Strategies for enhancing silicone’s potential in sustainable and industrially relevant biocatalysis are also discussed.


Silicone-based polymers are emerging as a highly promising yet underexplored platform for enzyme immobilization in synthetic biocatalysis. Combining exceptional thermal stability, chemical inertness, biocompatibility, and tunable properties, silicones are particularly well-suited for robust and reusable biocatalysts in both batch and continuous processes. This review provides a comprehensive overview of reported strategies for silicone-supported enzyme immobilization, including attachment, entrapment, and composite formation. Silicone matrices have demonstrated unique advantages in organic and multiphase systems by enhancing enzyme stability, reducing leaching, and improving mechanical resilience. Recent developments, such as silCoat composites and hydrophilized silicone formulations, have extended the applicability of these materials across a broader range of enzyme classes and reaction conditions. However, challenges remain, including mass transfer limitations for hydrophilic substrates, limited research beyond lipase-based systems, and scalability in industrial applications. By addressing these challenges, silicone-based immobilization could play a pivotal role in advancing sustainable and efficient chemical synthesis, merging the versatility of enzymatic catalysis with the robustness of advanced polymeric materials.

item.title: Electro‐Organocatalytic Synthesis: Recent Advances in Asymmetric Aminocatalysis, NHC Catalysis, and Beyond
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

This review highlights recent advances in electro-organocatalytic synthesis, focusing on the integration of electrochemical activation with organocatalysis, including aminocatalysis, N-heterocyclic carbene catalysis, and related catalytic strategies. The graphical abstract illustrates how electrochemical oxidation generates reactive intermediates that undergo asymmetric and non-asymmetric transformations under organocatalytic control.


This mini review provides a comprehensive and pedagogical overview of recent advances, primarily reported after 2020, in organocatalytic electrosynthetic strategies that merge organocatalysis with redox-mediated electroactivation. Progress in this rapidly evolving field demonstrates the ability of electro-organocatalysis to enable efficient access to structurally complex molecules through both asymmetric and non-asymmetric transformations while promoting greener, more selective, and sustainable synthetic approaches. The review discusses reaction optimization, substrate scope and limitations, mechanistic insights, and future perspectives, highlighting the significant potential of electro-organocatalysis as a versatile platform for further methodological innovation.

item.title: Dichloramine B: A Reagent for Regioselective Chloroalkoxylation of 3‐Aryloxindoles
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A catalyst/additive-free direct chloroalkoxylation of 3-aryloxindoles is achieved with dichloramine B as the chlorinating reagent and alcohols as nucleophiles.


A catalyst- and additive-free strategy for the direct chloroalkoxylation of 3-aryloxindoles has been developed using dichloramine B as a readily available electrophilic chlorinating reagent and alcohols as alkoxy nucleophiles. Notably, dichloramine B is converted to benzenesulfonamide during the chloroalkoxylation process, which is regenerated to dichloramine B with Cl2 in industry. This mild, operationally simple protocol affords aromatic-chloro-3-alkoxyoxindoles with excellent regioselectivity and broad functional-group tolerance.

item.title: Direct Access to Polyannulated Azacyclics Through a Cascade Double Annulation of Allenamines Triggered by Friedel–Crafts Alkylation and Nucleophilic Substitution
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A direct synthesis of poly-fused azacyclics bearing an all-carbon quaternary center from propargyl alcohols (PAs) and 2-pyrrolyl anilines has been developed, catalyzed by Sc(OTf)3 under solvent-free conditions. This approach involves the cascade double annulation of in situ-formed allenamines via an intramolecular Friedel–Crafts reaction, followed by 6-exo-tet cyclization. Further, the substrate scope, gram-scale synthesis, and mechanistic studies of the protocol were demonstrated.


Here, we report a direct synthesis of polyfused azacyclics bearing an all-carbon quaternary center from propargyl alcohols (PAs) and 2-pyrrolyl anilines, catalyzed by Sc(OTf)3 under solvent-free conditions. This approach involves the cascade double annulation of in situ-formed allenamines via an intramolecular Friedel–Crafts reaction, followed by 6-exo-tet cyclization. We demonstrated the substrate scope, gram-scale synthesis, and mechanistic studies of the protocol.

item.title: Recent Advances in Photocatalytic Difunctionalization and Hydrofunctionalization of Gem‐Difluorostyrenes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The visible-light-induced photoredox catalysis has triggered intensive progress on molecular synthesis, which also provides broader opportunities for sustainable difunctionalization of gem-difluorostyrenes. This review summarizes key advances in this field from the past decade, covering oxygenation, amination, fluorination, sulfonylation, hydrofunctionalization, and cycloadditions among related reactions.


The difunctionalization and hydrofunctionalization of gem-difluorostyrenes represent highly efficient approaches for the one-step construction of diverse fluorine-containing functional molecules, which hold significant application value in the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and functional materials. Photocatalysis, featuring mild reaction conditions, and unique radical reaction pathways, provides a green and efficient synthetic strategy for these transformations. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in the photocatalytic difunctionalization and hydrofunctionalization of gem-difluorostyrenes, including related cyclization reactions, with an emphasis on method development, substrate scope, synthetic applications, and limitations, as well as the mechanisms of these reactions.

item.title: Base‐Catalyzed Unexpected Cyclization of β‐Trifluoromethyl 2′‐Hydroxychalcones: Novel Synthesis of 2‐Substituted Benzofuran‐3(2H)‐Ones
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The presence of the trifluoromethyl group in the β-position of 2’-hydroxychalcones changes the direction of the cyclization process. DBU-catalyzed reaction of β-trifluoromethyl 2’-hydroxychalcones provides regioselectively 2-substituted α-trifluoromethyl-benzyl benzofuran-3(2H)-ones, typically in good yields under mild conditions.


The introduction of a trifluoromethyl group into the β-position of 2′-hydroxychalcones completely changes the direction of the cyclization process. DBU-catalyzed reaction of β-trifluoromethyl 2′-hydroxychalcones under mild conditions provides regioselectively 2-substituted α-trifluoromethyl-benzyl benzofuran-3(2H)-ones, typically in good yields (80%–93% after 0.5 h) and dr close to 4:1. However, relatively small changes in substrate structure at the β-position, e.g., replacement of CF3 with CF2H or a phenyl with a cyclohexyl group, lead to the formation of chroman-4-one framework. Moreover, 2′-hydroxychalcones containing CF2Cl or CF2CF3 group cyclize to a five-membered ring with elimination of hydrogen halide. Results of DFT calculations explain the reaction course and how the selectivity of the reaction is influenced by electronics and geometries of the substrates, intermediates, and transition states.

item.title: Metal Hydroxide Organic Frameworks: Design Principles and Applications in Electrocatalytic Oxidation
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The graphical abstract illustrates the rational design of catalytic sites in metal hydroxide organic frameworks (MHOFs) and the resulting structure–activity relationships in electrocatalytic oxidation. By integrating tunable organic linkers with layered metal hydroxide (LMH) frameworks, the local coordination environment, interlayer spacing, electronic structure, and accessibility of active metal sites can be precisely regulated. Organic linker engineering further modulates intermediate adsorption, proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), charge transfer, and structural reconstruction under electrochemical conditions. These synergistic effects optimize catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability across various electrooxidation reactions. The schematic highlights how molecular-level structural regulation provides fundamental design principles for developing efficient and durable MHOF electrocatalysts.


Electrocatalysts play a central role in electrochemical energy storage and conversion technologies; however, their practical applications are often hindered by structural degradation and active site deactivation under operating conditions. Therefore, achieving high catalytic activity while maintaining long-term structural stability remains a persistent challenge in catalyst design. Metal hydroxide organic frameworks (MHOFs), an emerging class of hybrid materials that integrate metal hydroxide layers with tunable organic linkers, have attracted increasing attention owing to their structural robustness, compositional versatility, and highly adjustable electronic environments. In electrocatalytic oxidation reactions, MHOFs provide opportunities to overcome the limitations of conventional catalysts through the synergistic regulation of hydroxide layers and organic ligands, thereby optimizing intermediate adsorption, interfacial configurations, and charge transfer pathways. Over the past several years, these features have enabled substantial improvements in electrocatalytic activity and durability. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in MHOF electrocatalysts, with a particular focus on structural classification, synthetic strategies, and structure performance relationships that govern electrocatalytic behavior. Particular attention is devoted to elucidating the mechanistic roles of hydroxide layer engineering and ligand modulation in regulating catalytic processes. Finally, current challenges, unresolved mechanistic questions, and future opportunities are discussed to provide design principles for next-generation MHOF electrocatalysts and facilitate their practical implementation.

item.title: Three‐Component Defluorinative Annulation of Polyfluoroalkyl Tetralones, Amidines, and Cobalt‐Dionates: Synthesis of Fluoro‐Alkyl 4‐(furan‐2‐yl)quinazolines
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

An unprecedented defluorinative multicomponent reaction of polyfluoroalkyl ketones, amidines, and cobalt-dionates is developed for the modular synthesis of structurally unique fluoroalkyl 4-(furan-2-yl)quinazolines.


An unprecedented defluorinative multicomponent reaction of polyfluoroalkyl ketones, amidines, and cobalt-dionates is developed for the modular synthesis of structurally unique fluoroalkyl 4-(furan-2-yl)quinazolines. The reaction proceeds through selective activation of six aliphatic CF bonds on three sterically congested polyfluoroalkylcarbon sites, therefore eliminating the classical reliance on multistep prefunctionalization and transition-metal-catalyzed couplings. Cobalt-dionates are used as versatile 1,3-dicarbonyl surrogates in the [3 + 2]-annulation, wherein key fluoroalkenyl intermediates are involved. Moreover, the reaction features good compatibility with various functional groups and applicability in postfunctionalization of the resulting heteroaromatics.

item.title: Recent Progress in the Synthesis of Sulfonylmethyl Compounds Using Diverse Sulfonylmethylating Reagents
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

This review outlines significant advances in sulfonylmethylation reactions employing key reagents such as methylarylsulfones, halogenated methyl sulfones, sulfonylmethyl isocyanide, and the combination of C1 synthons with sulfone sources as sulfonylmethylating agents. Furthermore, the corresponding reaction mechanisms are discussed.


Sulfonylmethyl motif is widely present in many organic compounds and has shown important application in pharmaceutical chemistry, organic synthesis, and materials science. In recent years, considerable attention has been devoted to the development of efficient methods for constructing sulfonylmethyl-containing compounds. This review focuses on summarizing the research progress from 2010 to 2025 in the synthesis of sulfonylmethyl compounds via various sulfonylmethylating reagents, including methylarylsulfones, halogenated methyl sulfones, and sulfonylmethyl isocyanide, as well as the coupling of C1 synthons with sulfone sources. Representative reaction modes and related mechanistic aspects are also discussed. This review aims to provide a systematic overview and useful reference for the further development and application of sulfonylmethylation chemistry.

item.title: Alkoxyallenes in Modern Synthesis: Reactivity, Catalysis, and Complexity Generation
item.description: The last decade has witnessed a remarkable transformation in alkoxyallene chemistry. Although historically employed as synthetic equivalents of acrolein or as versatile 3C synthons, alkoxyallenes are now increasingly recognized as highly adaptable platforms for synthetic design. The combination of a polarized cumulene framework, multiple chemically addressable carbon atoms, and diverse activation modes has enabled these substrates to engage in highly selective bond-forming processes across a broad range of reaction manifolds. This review discusses the conceptual and mechanistic advances that have shaped the field, emphasizing how complementary activation strategies can unlock distinct reactivity patterns within the alkoxyallene framework. Recent developments in transition-metal catalysis, radical chemistry, photochemistry, and metallaphotoredox activation have substantially expanded the reactivity profile of these substrates, while the continuing development of lithiated alkoxyallene chemistry has reinforced the exceptional versatility of this class of compounds. Beyond reaction development, the growing use of alkoxyallenes in total synthesis and polymer science underscores their evolution from specialized reactive intermediates into versatile building blocks for both molecular complexity generation and materials-oriented synthesis. Collectively, these studies demonstrate how alkoxyallene chemistry never stopped to reinvent itself, with new activation modes and catalytic strategies steadily expanding the opportunities available to these versatile substrates.

item.title: Selective Hydrogenation of α,β‐Unsaturated aldehydes to Unsaturated alcohols: From Metal Nanoparticles to Nanoclusters and Single‐Atom Catalysts
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)


The selective hydrogenation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes is a pivotal process for synthesizing fine chemicals, fragrances, and pharmaceuticals. However, achieving high chemoselectivity to unsaturated alcohols remains a significant challenge due to the thermodynamic and kinetic preference for CC bond hydrogenation over CO bond reduction. To address this, various strategies for modulating the electronic and geometric structures of the supported metal catalysts have been developed. Recent advances demonstrate that downsizing the size of metal nanoparticles (NPs) to nanoclusters (NCs) or even single atoms (SAs) could effectively tune the substrate mode and reaction pathways, thereby enhancing activity, selectivity, and stability. In this review, we summarize recent progress in the selective hydrogenation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes into unsaturated alcohols over supported NPs, NCs, and SAs, with emphasis on the influence of the electronic and geometric structures of active sites on catalytic performance. Finally, we discuss current challenges and provide prospective on the rational design of efficient heterogeneous catalysts for this transformation.

item.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed [4 + 2] Annulative Coupling Between 1,3‐Butadienes and 2‐Haloarylsulfonamides: En‐Route to Benzosultam Scaffolds
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A palladium-catalyzed [4 + 2] annulative Heck–Tsuji–Trost strategy to construct benzosultams directly from 2-halo-arylsulfonamides and abundant feedstock material 1,3-butadienes is studied. The strategic design accommodates a broad substrate scope with excellent functional group compatibility and wide synthetic transformations, delivering structurally diverse and pharmaceutically relevant sultam scaffolds.


Herein, we have demonstrated a palladium-catalyzed [4 + 2] annulation reaction to acquire benzosultam frameworks from readily accessible 2-iodo-arylsulfonamides and feedstock material 1,3-butadienes. The synthetic transformation involves consecutive CC and CN bond formations by following intermolecular Heck-type coupling and intramolecular Tsuji–Trost allylic amination via a transient π-allyl-Pd-intermediate to enable benzosultams. Operational simplicity, broad substrate scope, viability of functional groups, scalability, and further synthetic transformations are the significance of the protocol.

item.title: Thiocarbonyl‐Directed Rhodium‐Catalyzed C2‐Selective C─H Bond Activation and Cyclization of N,N‐Dimethylthioamide Indoles With Alkynes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The thiocarbonyl-directed rhodium-catalyzed C2-selective C─H bond activation and cyclization of N,N-dimethylthioamide indoles with alkynes have been developed for the synthesis of substituted pyrrolo[1,2-a]indole-3-thiones. This [3 + 2] cyclization exhibits the retention of thiocarbonyl and differs from previous thiocarbonyl-directed C─H bond activation reactions which typically only reflect the coupling of different components.


The thiocarbonyl-directed rhodium-catalyzed C2-selective C─H bond activation and cyclization of N,N-dimethylthioamide indoles with alkynes have been proposed, resulting in the efficient production of a series of substituted pyrrolo[1,2-a]indole-3-thiones. The synthetic potential and mechanism of this strategy have also been preliminarily investigated. This protocol possesses the following advantages: stable and easily available substrates, redox-neutral and concise conditions, precise C2-selective C─H functionalization of indoles, and cyclic products with the retention of thiocarbonyl.

item.title: Calcium(II)‐Catalyzed Alkoxyselenation of 1,3‐Dienes With Selenium–Nitrogen Exchange Reagents
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A calcium(II)-catalyzed three-component alkoxyselenation of 1,3-dienes with benzothiaselenazole-1-oxides and alcohols has been developed. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions and enables efficient construction of diverse organoselenium compounds with excellent chemo-, regio-, and E-selectivity. Broad substrate compatibility, late-stage functionalization, gram-scale synthesis, and downstream derivatization demonstrate the synthetic utility of this practical selenium–nitrogen exchange-based strategy.


Organoselenium compounds are widely found in biologically active molecules and functional materials, yet efficient and selective selenofunctionalization of conjugated dienes remains underdeveloped. Herein, we report a calcium(II)-catalyzed three-component alkoxyselenation of 1,3-dienes with benzothiaselenazole-1-oxides (BTSAs), a class of selenium–nitrogen exchange reagents, and alcohols as nucleophiles. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions and provides straightforward access to structurally diverse organoselenium compounds in moderate to good yields with excellent chemo-, regio-, and E-selectivity. A broad range of aryl-, heteroaryl-, and alkyl-substituted 1,3-dienes, as well as structurally diverse BTSAs and alcohols, are well tolerated. The synthetic utility of this protocol is further demonstrated by late-stage functionalization of complex molecules, gram-scale synthesis, and downstream derivatization, highlighting its potential as a practical platform for the synthesis and diversification of bioactive organoselenium compounds.

item.title: A General Electrochemical Platform for Dehydrazinative Oxygenation of Hydrazines
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

This study presents a catalyst-free electrochemical protocol at room temperature, using anodic oxidation to drive the dehydrazinative C─O coupling of hydrazines with TEMPO, affording diverse products in good yields with broad functional group compatibility and scalability.


Herein, we disclose an electrochemical protocol that operates under catalyst-free conditions at room temperature, enabling the dehydrazinative oxygenation of hydrazines with TEMPO. This straightforward approach relies on anodic oxidation to initiate a radical pathway, furnishing a diverse array of C─O coupling products in satisfactory yields. The transformation accommodates a wide range of hydrazine derivatives, showcasing outstanding tolerance toward various functional groups. The preparative utility of this method is further demonstrated by late-stage functionalization of bioactive compounds, gram-scale reactions, and subsequent product modifications. Mechanistic studies indicate that the process proceeds through an electrochemically driven radical coupling pathway.

item.title: Transition Metal‐Free Vinylcyclopropanation of Olefins via Carbolithiation Reactions: Synthesis of 3‐Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexanes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Readily accessible N-allyl-N-2-bromoallylamines undergo a tandem lithiation–cyclization cascade to furnish highly substituted 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexanes. The transformation proceeds without transition metals and delivers products with excellent diastereocontrol across a broad substrate range. Theoretical studies clarify the factors governing stereoselectivity and explain unusual selectivity trends through alternative transition-state conformations.


A formal vinylcyclopropanation of olefins from N-allyl N-(3-alkoxymethyl-2-lithioallyl) amines acting as carbenoid equivalents is described. The reaction proceeds through a tandem 5-exo carbolithiation/3-exo SNʹ affording 1-vinylazabicyclo[3.1.0]hexanes. Different substituents can be located at any of the other positions of the azabicycle, leading in most cases to high diastereoselectivities. DFT studies have been performed to account for the observed stereoselectivities that could not be rationalized in all cases through the expected chair-like transition states.

item.title: Electrochemical C(sp2)─H Amination of Benzoxazoles Using Liquid DMF as a Safe and Practical Dimethylamino Source
item.description: A novel and environmentally benign electrochemical method for the direct C2─H amination of benzoxazoles has been developed. This protocol employs N, N-dimethylformamide not only as a solvent but also as the amino source, undergoing anodic decarbonylation to generate a dimethylamino radical. The reaction proceeds under exogenous oxidant- and transition metal-free conditions, utilizing inexpensive iodine as a redox mediator and a catalytic amount of 4-tert-butylbenzoic acid as an additive. A broad range of substituted benzoxazoles is tolerated, affording the corresponding 2-(dimethylamino)benzoxazole derivatives in moderate to good yields. The transformation shows excellent functional group compatibility and is scalable to gram-level. Mechanistic investigations, including radical trapping experiments and cyclic voltammetry, support a radical pathway involving the key formation of a dimethylamino radical intermediate.

item.title: Unveiling the Microkinetic Origin of Negative Impedance in Oxygen Reduction Electrocatalysis: A Pulse‐Potential Strategy for Enhanced Activity
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Microkinetic model reveals that negative impedance in ORR originates from OHad relaxation, enabling EIS-guided pulse-potential design for enhanced activity.


By developing a microkinetic model for the associative oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), we reveal that negative impedance in electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) arises under specific combinations of electrode potential and hydroxyl binding energy (ΔGOH${\unicode[Arial]{x0394}} \boldsymbol{G}_{\mathbf{OH}}$). This phenomenon stems from dynamic competition between intermediate adsorption/desorption and charge transfer, with the OHad$\mathbf{OH}_{\mathbf{ad}}$ coverage relaxation playing a dominant role. Crucially, the frequency range of negative impedance is correlated with the intrinsic timescale of the coverage relaxation and can serve as a guide for selecting the perturbation frequency in pulse-potential experiments. We thus establish an impedance-guided dynamic modulation framework and demonstrate that applying a square-wave potential pulse with this optimal frequency window can selectively enhance the time-averaged ORR current by dynamically mitigating adsorbate poisoning. This work bridges EIS signatures to ORR microkinetics and establishes a general, impedance-guided framework for rationally designing pulsed-potential protocols. This approach transforms EIS from a passive diagnostic tool into an active design compass for boosting catalytic performance beyond static limits.
